name: Pontederia

project_scope.mode: genus lesson only; no canonical installation

shared_genus_traits: Aquatic perennial monocots with six-lobed tubular perianths and six unequal stamens.
Flowers in spathe-associated spikes; broad long-petiolate leaves may be emergent or floating.
Modern Pontederia includes former Eichhornia crassipes; these are not two separate species.
look_here_first: TRACE THE ROOTS: rooted rhizome in mud with erect leaves = P. cordata; usually free-floating rosette with dangling feathery roots and spongy petioles = P. crassipes. Confirm with spike flower count and fruit.

species_comparison_matrix.crassipes: Usually free-floating, feathery pendant roots; may root secondarily.

species_comparison_matrix.cordata: Erect flowering stems and emergent leaves.
Not bulbously inflated; constricted immediately below blade.
species_comparison_matrix.crassipes: Spongy, often swollen or bulbous; may be elongated and less inflated in dense mats.

species_comparison_matrix.cordata: Densely many-flowered; up to several hundred.
Upper central lobe with a two-lobed yellow mark.
species_comparison_matrix.crassipes: Upper lobe with dark blotch enclosing yellow mark.

species_comparison_matrix.cordata: One-seeded utricle enclosed by toothed-ridged persistent perianth.

field_steps: 1. Check rooted versus free-floating habit without disturbing the plant.
2. Photograph mature petiole and rosette/stem with scale.
3. Count buds, open flowers and scars across an entire spike.
4. Measure perianth lobe, not just flower diameter.
5. Confirm with mature fruit anatomy; if missing, use combined vegetative and floral characters.
overlap_cautions: Both have six-part flowers and can bloom blue-violet; color is not diagnostic.
P. cordata leaf shapes vary widely; a broad blade alone is not water-hyacinth.
Crowded P. crassipes may have long, less swollen petioles; inspect roots and spike.
Detached or deep-water plants can obscure rooting; do not force ID.
Eichhornia crassipes is a synonym of P. crassipes in POWO, not another canonical card.
Native-range certification is separate from source-pool learner admission.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.separator: Canonical Pontederiaceae relative with narrow aquatic leaves, solitary yellow flower and 3 stamens; not a broad-leaved dense-spiked Pontederia.
Source-pool arrowheads with three distinct petals and achene heads, not six-lobed tubular Pontederia flowers and their fruit.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Same-scale field views, arrows to rhizome attachment vs hanging roots.
Macro with scale, arrow to below-blade constriction vs spongy swelling.
Whole inflorescences with scale and bud/flower counts.
Matched dissections: toothed-ridged one-seeded utricle vs 3-valved capsule.
Multiple mature leaf outlines and bases, same scale.
Compare open-water bulbous and crowded elongate petioles.
Annotate solitary vs dense flowers and 3 petals vs 6 lobes.

handoffs.task: Acquire exact-species licensed root, petiole, spike and fruit photos with provenance; visual-incomplete.
Both sheet-backed species absent from manifest on 2026-10-12; install separately only after identity gate; Eichhornia is an alias.
Preserve POWO Pontederia crassipes / Eichhornia crassipes mapping and independently label native-range state.
